chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who marries off his daughter: Is it for him to eat her dowry? He said, 'No, it is not for him.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلُ: Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (Imam Musa al-Kazim, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Does a father have the right to keep his daughter's dowry when he arranges her marriage?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Hasan al-Muthanna (AS) clarifies that the father does not automatically own the dowry (mahr) given for his daughter, establishing her exclusive right to it. This ruling underscores the principle that mahr is the bride's personal property, distinct from the father's guardianship role in the marriage contract. It serves as a foundational legal precedent in Shia jurisprudence for protecting women's financial rights within the marital union.
